transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi. Honestly, what finally pushed me to come in is that... well, my shoulders and neck just stay clenched all day. It's like I'm constantly bracing for a classroom observation that never ends. And by the evening, my jaw aches so badly that I can hardly even enjoy playing my guitar anymore. The physical tension is just constant, and I needed to get it checked out.
Do you find yourself feeling anxious or worried about things throughout the day, even when there's no specific reason for it?

Yes, pretty much constantly. My mind just keeps circling from one thing to the next. I'll worry about whether I'll ever get hired again, or... or if I've completely ruined my reputation with the parents. Then I'll start stressing that my retirement is slipping away. It even gets down to really small things—like, I'll agonize over whether a tiny mistake I made during a story-time activity means I shouldn't even be trusted with children anymore. It's just a constant loop of worrying.
Do you feel like you can't control or stop the worrying, even when you try?

Yes, exactly. I mean, I really try to stop it. I'll tell myself to just make a list of things to do, or I'll try to pray, or go out and weed the garden... just trying to focus on the next practical step, you know? But it doesn't work. One worry just hands off to another, and before I know it, I've lost half the afternoon just sitting there, completely stuck in my head. I just can't seem to shut it off.
Do you notice any other physical symptoms like muscle tension, headaches, or stomach issues that also seem to be related to this constant worrying?

Well, like I mentioned earlier, the muscle tension is definitely the biggest thing... my neck and shoulders are just always tight, and my jaw aches. But as far as other things... I don't really get headaches, and my stomach seems fine, honestly. It's really just that constant tightness in my muscles.
